chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
From the blessings of the woman is the lightness of her expenditure and the ease of her childbirth, and from her misfortune is the heaviness of her expenditure and the difficulty of her childbirth.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of a blessed woman according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links a woman's domestic ease to her spiritual state, reflecting the Shia concept of 'barakah' as a tangible divine grace manifesting in physical and economic well-being. It serves as both a diagnostic tool for assessing marital compatibility and a reminder that ease in provision and childbirth are signs of God's favor, while difficulty may indicate spiritual or social misalignment.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘It is from the Blessings of the woman the lightness of her expenditure and the ease of her giving birth, and from her misfortune the intensity of her expenditure and the difficulties of her giving birth’.
en.sarwar: 37. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “
Of the blessing of a woman is her being of light expenses and her giving birth with ease. Of the evil with her is intensified expenses and her giving birth with hardships and difficulties.’”
